problemStatement.formal: \limsup_{n\to\infty} f(n)/n = \infty,\ \text{where } f(n) \text{ is the least } m \ge 1 \text{ with } n \in \mathrm{partialDivisorSums}(m).
problemStatement.plain: Let f(n) be the least m for which n appears as a partial sum of the smallest divisors of m. Does f(n)/n grow without bound (limsup = ∞)?
whyMatters: Connects representability by partial divisor sums to Goldbach's conjecture
Tao's work suggests f(n)/n can be large; the limsup question probes the sharp growth rate
